title: Microsoft Purview DLP: remediation actions inside email notifications
summary: Hold: the PowerShell reference lists the remediation parameter but does not document what it sets, so the proposed automation is not verified. The policy creation path omits a required template choice, and the assurance that external parties cannot use the actions is not supported. The roadmap facts and the documented notification actions otherwise check out.

claims.claim: The creation route to notification settings contains a single Custom choice after Enterprise applications & devices.
claims.quote: Select Custom from both the Categories list and the Regulations list.
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Custom (Categories) > Custom (Regulations) > Create or customize advanced DLP rules > + Create rule > User Notifications > Preview and edit notification email'. The final button is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-use-notifications-and-policy-tips, which is already cited. Retain the note that actions are selected when configuring that email.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions <value> configures the remediation actions offered by notification emails.
claims.quote: Searched: "NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions"; Purview DLP actionable email notifications licensing price meter NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions external recipients. Opened Set-DlpComplianceRule: the parameter has a type and a placeholder description, but no documented effect.
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to null and remove its rendered call. Retain only the existing note that the reference lists -NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions without explaining what it sets; do not present it as verified automation for this control.

claims.claim: The Set-DlpComplianceRule reference lists NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions but does not describe its effect.
claims.quote: Searched: "NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions". Opened and searched Set-DlpComplianceRule for that parameter and Identity: its description is '{{ Fill NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions Description }}'; search excerpts for New-DlpComplianceRule also give no effect.

claims.claim: Audit > Search in the Microsoft Purview portal reaches audit search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. ... On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog is a read-only audit search command run in Exchange Online PowerShell, not a command to restrict or reverse remediation.
claims.quote: The underlying cmdlet used to search the audit log is an Exchange Online cmdlet, which is Search-UnifiedAuditLog. ... You have to run this cmdlet in Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Audit search requires the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. ... To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.where: Scope: Clouds and platform; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited notification page names no cloud for these actions.
claims.quote: Searched: "actionable email notifications" override permissions recovery GCC automation. Read the full dlp-use-notifications-and-policy-tips page; it specifies OneDrive and SharePoint workloads but no GCC, GCC High, DoD or other cloud availability.

claims.claim: The notification page does not describe recovery after Delete file.
claims.quote: Searched: "actionable email notifications" override permissions recovery GCC automation. Read the full notifications page: it says 'Delete file: Deletes the file', without a recovery procedure.

claims.claim: No source says existing notification emails automatically acquire actions without administrator configuration.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP actionable email notifications licensing price meter NotifyEmailOnedriveRemediationActions external recipients. Read roadmap and notifications page; the latter says admins select the options when configuring emails, not that existing emails change automatically.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist tells readers to check audit ingestion, but the controls table contains only remediation configuration and audit record search.
claims.quote: Confirm that audit log search is on by running Get-AdminAuditLogConfig ... Table rows: 'Which remediation actions a DLP rule's email notification offers to users'; 'Audit records of actions users take from notification emails'.

claims.claim: The risk rating is Medium even though the verified admin-opt-in capability exposes no new actions until an admin configures it.
claims.quote: defaultState: "admin-opt-in"; risk: "medium"; rationale: 'Medium. Users can delete a file, remove its sharing or override the policy from an email'. The scale rates nothing happening until admin opt-in as low.
claims.fix: Set risk to 'low' and replace its rationale with 'Low. The remediation actions are unavailable until an admin selects them in the notification configuration. Before opting in, review destructive actions and recipients because notification emails are sent unprotected.'

claims.claim: No agent or automated remediation is described for these user-operated email actions.
claims.quote: Searched: "actionable email notifications" override permissions recovery GCC automation. Read the full notifications page; its actionable-notifications section describes controls that users operate directly from email, not an agent or automated remediation.
